text:
Nikita Kucherov is in the last year of his contract, has asked out of Tampa and has heard the general manager say no. On Sunday his line sat for part of the third period of a 6-2 loss to Buffalo. So the Lightning welcome the Stanley Cup champions with more eyes on one man's bench demeanour than on the standings. The headlines have started asking whether winning could change his mind. Our numbers have him at 40% for two or more points, the best on either side.

Tampa gets help tonight. Brandon Hagel, 24 points in 20 games before he went on injured reserve, has been activated, and Zemgus Girgensons is expected back too. Hagel is our likeliest Lightning scorer at 39%. Conor Geekie is gone for four to five months after shoulder surgery. The process has held all season (56% of the five-on-five expected goals, the quality of chances each side gets), and Andrei Vasilevskiy at +2.1 goals saved above expected after a +23.2 season is most of the gap between good and frightening.

Carolina has points in seven straight (6-0-1) and took 62% of the expected goals in that run. The results run a little ahead even of that dominance, with 6.0 goals of extra finishing and 7.4 from goaltending, but that goaltending hasn't come from tonight's starter. Brandon Bussi gets the net over Pyotr Kochetkov, and Bussi is at .879 and 1.6 goals worse than expected in nine games. That's the one soft spot in a team that otherwise looks like it never left June.

Nikolaj Ehlers is out, so Taylor Hall, honored last week for 1,000 games, has moved up beside Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake. Stankoven has 13 points in ten. Sebastian Aho is our likeliest Hurricane at 32% to score. The Hurricanes are effectively in already; Tampa is 96%, and the more interesting race is whether Kucherov's season stays about hockey.
headline: Kucherov's Lightning meet the champions, Hagel returns
